items.title: Lanny Morgan interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 14, 1999
items.q: the saxes when I joined were Frank Hittner was playing baritone and Joe Farrell was playing tenor and Willie and myself

ctx.x: I’m serious. And I couldn’t do it. Because I moved, I like to say lock, stock and barrel to New York. I didn’t have that much then, I was, well it was right around my 26th birthday. But I had canceled everything out there and moved to New York. And then he wanted me to come on the band. So I had to turn him down. So it was really a drag. But the band then, I have to say that I did the right thing. Because, talking about Maynard’s band again, I think Stan’s band never really achieved what it once was. Maybe after…

don’t think it was ever that again. And Maynard’s band was on the rise and it was a hot band and it just kept getting better and better. And so many guys went through that band. You know the saxes when I joined were Frank Hittner was playing baritone and Joe Farrell was playing tenor and Willie and myself. Slide Hampton was on the band quite a bit off and on, Jackie Byard, and then a lot of other guys came through the band too at different times.
Were you there when Don Menza came through?
